source.title: On a continuous time model of gradient descent dynamics and instability in deep learning
source.authors: Mihaela Rosca; Yan Wu; C. Qin; Benoit Dherin

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether controlling discretization drift changes test performance, using DAL-p sweeps and test accuracy rather than the versions’ specified interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-performance results for drift-controlled training. Its edge-of-stability results and cited findings about generalization are not separate rows unless the paper itself reports an outcome relevant to the claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures discretization drift, training stability, Hessian eigenvalues and DAL-p test performance, but does not test any specified claim version. Its flatness results do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or generalization gaps. Comparisons across batch sizes do not establish V5's fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the generalization results. The authors conclude that DAL enables stable training and that greater discretization drift is associated with increased generalization performance. Their broader contribution is a principal flow that captures oscillatory and unstable gradient-descent dynamics. They acknowledge that the largest Hessian eigenvalue could confound the drift–generalization association.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes principal flow and drift-adjusted learning rates; it does not reproduce the listed original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: DAL-p power controls the amount of drift; the paper reports test-performance trends across power values, datasets and batch-size settings.

fits_no_version.finding: DAL-p sweeps associate greater discretization drift with higher test accuracy. DAL-0.125 matches SGD at 86% on CIFAR-10 with batch size 64, improves full-batch CIFAR-10 accuracy from 77% to 82%, and improves ImageNet accuracy from 42% to 50% with batch size 8192. The authors also report flatter learned landscapes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlling discretization drift through learning-rate adaptation changes training stability and test performance; greater drift correlates with better test accuracy in the reported settings.

record.problems: The drift–test-performance relationship is reported as a correlation and the authors note the largest Hessian eigenvalue could confound it. Several sweep values are figure-only in the supplied text. The reported comparisons do not directly measure training-to-test error gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible test-performance rows identified. DAL and DAL-0.5 comparisons in Figures 18–20 and 41–45 are not extracted because they compare specific training recipes rather than reporting the drift-to-test-performance sweep or explicit test-accuracy comparisons used here.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and held-out performance against natural-label training with the same architecture and recipe.
No width sweep beyond the width required to interpolate.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.

No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under the specified tuning conditions. DAL-p primarily adapts a global learning rate; the preliminary per-parameter experiments do not supply the required comparison.
No established large- versus small-batch comparison under a fixed epoch budget. The batch-size experiments show iteration curves and method comparisons.

No magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure, ranking of training-to-test gaps, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Hessian eigenvalues and landscape visualizations measure different quantities.
No removal of memorized training examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows belong under fits_no_version rather than claim-testing evidence. Their cannot_determine states concern the listed versions, not whether the reported accuracy improvements occurred. No additional result testing V1–V8 was identified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not compared.
No width sweep around the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No comparison of large and small batches under a fixed epoch budget.
Does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or rank training-to-test gaps. It reports drift and test accuracy, and discusses the largest Hessian eigenvalue and loss-landscape flatness.
